verses.text: Yahweh said to me, “Take a large tablet, and write on it with a man’s pen, ‘For Maher Shalal Hash Baz’;
and I will take for myself faithful witnesses to testify: Uriah the priest, and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah.”
I went to the prophetess, and she conceived, and bore a son. Then Yahweh said to me, “Call his name ‘Maher Shalal Hash Baz.’
For before the child knows how to say, ‘My father,’ and, ‘My mother,’ the riches of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria will be carried away by the king of Assyria.”
Yahweh spoke to me yet again, saying,
“Because this people have refused the waters of Shiloah that go softly, and rejoice in Rezin and Remaliah’s son;
now therefore, behold, the Lord brings upon them the mighty flood waters of the River: the king of Assyria and all his glory. It will come up over all its channels, and go over all its banks.
It will sweep onward into Judah. It will overflow and pass through; it will reach even to the neck; and the stretching out of its wings will fill the width of your land, Immanuel.
Make an uproar, you peoples, and be broken in pieces! Listen, all you from far countries: dress for battle, and be shattered! Dress for battle, and be shattered!
Take counsel together, and it will be brought to nothing; speak the word, and it will not stand: for God is with us.”
For Yahweh spoke thus to me with a strong hand, and instructed me not to walk in the way of this people, saying,
“Don’t say, ‘A conspiracy!’ concerning all about which this people say, ‘A conspiracy!’ neither fear their threats, nor be terrorized.
Yahweh of Armies is who you must respect as holy. He is the one you must fear. He is the one you must dread.
He will be a sanctuary, but for both houses of Israel, he will be a trap and a snare for the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
Many will stumble over it, fall, be broken, be snared, and be captured.”
Wrap up the testimony. Seal the law among my disciples.
I will wait for Yahweh, who hides his face from the house of Jacob, and I will look for him.
Behold, I and the children whom Yahweh has given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel from Yahweh of Armies, who dwells in Mount Zion.

When they tell you, “Consult with those who have familiar spirits and with the wizards, who chirp and who mutter:” shouldn’t a people consult with their God? Should they consult the dead on behalf of the living?
Turn to the law and to the testimony! If they don’t speak according to this word, surely there is no morning for them.
They will pass through it, very distressed and hungry; and it will happen that when they are hungry, they will worry, and curse by their king and by their God. They will turn their faces upward,
and look to the earth, and see distress, darkness, and the gloom of anguish. They will be driven into thick darkness.

footnotes.content: Isaiah is told to write a name on a tablet—'Maher Shalal Hash Baz,' meaning 'swift is plunder, speedy is prey.' It's a hard message, written large for all to see. God uses even a child's name as His word to Judah.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Uriah the priest and Zechariah—faithful witnesses to God's word. Sometimes the hardest truth comes with honest witnesses standing by. Their names matter because God's promise doesn't fade with time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A son born to Isaiah and his wife—not just a son, but a living sign. The child's very existence says what God is doing. He will grow up speaking words his parents once wrote in fear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Before the boy even learns to say Father or Mother—before innocence ends—Damascus and Samaria will fall. God is showing Judah that He moves history along His own timetable, not ours. Even our children become witnesses to His sovereignty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh speaks again—not once but yet again. When a father keeps speaking, it's because His children keep not listening. His patience with us is relentless.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The waters of Shiloah go softly—a gentle stream, the water supply that sustains Jerusalem. But Judah refuses this and instead 'rejoices in Rezin and Remaliah's son'—trusting Syria over the silent, faithfully flowing God. We so often choose noise over nourishment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now comes the flood—the king of Assyria, his might and glory poured out like a mighty river. When we refuse God's gentle waters, He allows our own choices to rise like floodwaters. He doesn't stop loving; He allows us to see where our worship has gone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The flood will reach even to the neck—almost drowning Judah. And then: 'Immanuel'—the name breaks through in the darkness. God is with us. Even in the flood, even at the throat of judgment, the name of God's presence echoes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Let the nations rage, dress for battle, be shattered—the command is almost taunting. Nations plot and scheme, but God's word stands over them like the dawn over night. Our enemies are louder, but our God is sovereign.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'God is with us'—Immanuel again, the centerpiece. Take counsel, make plans, speak your word—none of it will stand if God is against it. But if God is with us, nothing can stand against us. This is the hinge the whole passage turns on.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: With a strong hand—God grabs Isaiah. Fear is spreading like the flood, but God's grip is stronger. He instructs Isaiah not to follow the way of Judah's frantic conspiracy-mongering. The hand that holds you speaks peace to your trembling heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't say 'A conspiracy!'—don't join the panic. Fear spreads fastest when we whisper its name. Isaiah is told to stand apart, to refuse the contagion of terror. Faithfulness looks like stubborn, quiet refusal to be swept away.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh of Armies is the one to respect as holy. He—not Assyria, not threats, not the panic of the city. When we have rightly feared the Lord, all other fears fall silent. Reverence for God is the antidote to terror.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He will be a sanctuary to those who trust Him, but a trap to those who stumble over Him. The same God is both refuge and stone of stumbling—depending on whether we lean on Him or reject Him. Grace and judgment rest in the same hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Many will stumble, fall, be broken, be snared. The warning is plain. Rejection of God isn't neutral; it has weight and consequence. But the name Immanuel has just been spoken. There is a way through.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Wrap up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples. When the flood comes and lies spread like fog, God's word is sealed among His learners. The true school is with those who have chosen to listen to Him. His word doesn't scatter; it gathers His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I will wait for Yahweh, who hides his face. Sometimes God's face is hidden—we cannot see the end, cannot trace His steps. Yet Isaiah commits to wait. This is not enthusiasm; it's loyalty to One who has earned it, even in darkness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I and the children whom Yahweh has given me are for signs and wonders. Isaiah's life, his son, his faithfulness—all of it is a sign to Israel. Sometimes being faithful means being a sign to others that God is real and near, even when the world makes no sense.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shouldn't a people consult with their God instead of chasing familiar spirits and wizards? When we're frightened, we reach for any comfort—spiritism, superstition, anything but the Living God. The question is gentle but urgent: why turn anywhere else?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Turn to the law and to the testimony!'—God's word is a lamp. If people don't speak according to God's word, there is no morning for them. This is the test: does what you're hearing align with what God has said? If not, you're walking deeper into darkness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Very distressed and hungry, they will curse by their king and by their God. Hunger and hardship reveal who a person truly trusts. And if they curse God when suffering comes, it shows they never truly knew Him—only expected His benefits.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Driven into thick darkness—the shadow of exile and judgment. Readers today hear an echo of how much we wander without the light of God's word. And yet Immanuel still stands, still present even in the darkest hour, inviting us home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
